findings.title: Her figure gets up on the view's clock, not the simulation's: drawn standing while her body still lies on the steel
findings.failure: _topple decides when she rises from DOWN_SECONDS for her current stage and down_s (down_for_s_, which only counts up). The simulation fixes how long she lies when the blow lands (down_s_ = down_seconds() at matron.cpp:2191), then adds kKnockdownRage at matron.cpp:2204. step_rage on the next tick can then move her up a stage. Example: a pest with rage of 0.37 or more is felled by a heaved toolbox. Rage goes past 0.45, so the view now has Dangerous and lie_s = 2.5, while the simulation keeps her down for 4.0 s. From 2.5 s on, k = 0. The figure is drawn upright, untoppled, still in the STATE_DOWN 'flat on the steel' pose (pitch 0, arms spread wide), for 1.5 s. Meanwhile the simulation still has a 0.6 m lying capsule there with no hands. Repeated knockdowns of a pest add 0.08 each, so one of them always crosses the line. Dangerous to Changed gives the same thing (view 1.2 s, simulation 2.5 s). The pinned case does too: room_to_stand(at) fails at matron.cpp:2346 and she crawls. down_for_s_ then passes lie_s, and she is drawn standing, often inside whatever pinned her, for as long as she crawls.
findings.fix: Let the simulation drive the rise. Export the time she has left (max(down_s_, 0)) and a pinned/crawling flag (Down with down_s_ <= 0) in View/MatronSnapshot/get_matron_state. In _topple, compute the rise from that remaining time, not from DOWN_SECONDS[stage], and keep k = 1 while she is pinned. Then the figure only stands when stand_up() actually runs.

findings.title: A stagger ends the Turn with no cooldown, so she starts a fresh wind-up the moment she recovers
findings.failure: The stagger branch of take_blow sets turn_ = None and turn_s_ = 0, but unlike the Down branch (2196) it never sets turn_cooldown_s_. During a Turn that value stays at 0. sight_far_s_ is not advanced or reset while she is Staggering, because step_turn is not called. Example: a Changed Matron in a lunge takes a blow she is facing (braced, so only staggered), or a dangerous one takes a hard enough chest blow (at least w*b, about 1.9 m/s crouched). When stagger_s_ runs out she goes back to Hunting. step_turn at 983/988 then sees cooldown 0, and sight_far_s_ is still 0.5 s or more while the player is within 13 m in sight. So she goes straight back into Windup and then a full 3.2 s Lunge. The stagger lengthens the Turn instead of breaking it, which goes against 'no Turn' while knocked.
findings.fix: In the stagger branch, when turn_ != None, set turn_cooldown_s_ = turn_cooldown_seconds() as the Down branch does, and reset sight_far_s_ = 0.

findings.title: Getting up sends her to re-search an old lead and counts it as being fooled again (she can reach 'fooled twice' from one noise)
findings.failure: stand_up() always sets state_ = Searching with the old heard_x_/heard_z_ and lead_seen_ as they were. It skips both the activity she was doing and the Hunting lose-track fix-up. Path: she hears a far noise, runs to it, finds nobody, searches for 8 s, ++fooled_ (now 1), stands down and goes to Guarding at her post. She is then knocked down at the post by something she did not see: a weight dropped from above, or a throw after which the player creeps out of sight during her 4 s on the steel. On rising she leaves the post, walks back to that same stale noise, searches another 8 s, and at 1488 does ++fooled_ again (now 2). From then on far noises no longer draw her off her post and every heard lead is approached as wary. A Shuffling Matron that is knocked down does the same, re-searching her release-time heard_x_.
findings.fix: After standing, resume what she was doing before (stand_down() for Guarding/Shuffling/Unrigging, or keep resume_state_), or search where she fell. If the Searching state stays, mark this search as not counting toward fooled_ (for example set lead_seen_ = true or use a 'risen' flag checked at 1487).

findings.title: A striker is accepted by being nearby, not by touching her, so things that pass close by knock her down
findings.failure: take_blow counts a body as a striker if four things hold: its speed changed by at least 0.1 m/s in the step, it was closing on her, and after the step its centre is within kRadius + its world-AABB half-diagonal + 0.25 m of her axis (about 1.14 m for a drum). It never checks that the body touched her. Gravity alone changes speed by 9.81/90 = 0.109 m/s per tick, so anything in flight passes the 0.1 'nothing met it' test. Any change the body gets from the floor, a rail or another body is then counted as her impulse (line 2098). Reproduced at c780427 with a scratch probe: a pest guarding at her post, and a 55 kg drum sent along the deck at shin height 0.75 m to her side (debug_launch_kit_body at her x+0.75, feet+0.46, z+1.0, velocity (0,0,-3.3)). The drum lands and skids past her, at least 0.3 m clear of her capsule; her own track shows no kick. Floor friction slows it from 3.29 to 2.19 m/s over 4 ticks, and that loss is counted as a 0.277 m/s blow. Its centre is under kLowBlowM, so reach is 0 and fells = takes = 0.245. Result: state Down, knockdowns 1, with no contact at all. A standing dangerous Matron has the same 0.245 threshold. Corpse ragdoll parts (object layer kCorpse, which never collides with her) are also candidates. Once any such body counts, her own velocity change from rails or the player's body that tick is added to blow_change_ as well.
findings.fix: Only accept a striker that actually touched her this step, e.g. `if (!physics_.WereBodiesInContact(body_, n.body)) continue;`. Jolt's PhysicsSystem has this, and it reads the step's contact cache. Alternatively, collide her capsule against the striker. Also remove gravity*dt from its_change before the 0.1 threshold, and skip bodies whose object layer cannot collide with hers.

findings.title: The load the player carries is not excluded, so carrying anything into her counts as a blow, including the player's own body
findings.failure: sense_near skips only her own body, the player's body and the stock in her own hands. The body the player carries is still a candidate. update_carry sets its velocity to the hands' every tick, before she senses, so it is always 'closing of its own motion' while the player moves toward her. Once it qualifies, blow_change_ += change (line 2137) also adds the change the player's body makes to her speed, and blow_quiet_ resets every tick it keeps pushing, so the total keeps growing. Reproduced at c780427, starting from the matron-heave setup: toolbox picked up, pest hunting within 4 m, player walking at her. (1) With her hands held off, the run_matron_collision setup: the same head-on meeting that gives knockdowns 0 empty-handed (closing 15 m/s) gives blow 3.34 m/s and puts her Down. (2) With her hands free: she is Down (blow 0.36) on the same tick as her shove. A pest, or a dangerous Matron while standing, is put down just by walking at her with a toolbox in hand, without throwing. This breaks the stated 'never the player's body' rule.
findings.fix: In sense_near, skip the body whose user data equals player_holding_ (set every tick before pre_step), the same way `held` is skipped. Do not add her own change to blow_change_ on a tick when the player's body is in contact with her (e.g. WereBodiesInContact(body_, player_)). Consider capping how many ticks a single contact can keep adding to the total.

findings.title: lie_down tests whether the lying capsule fits 0.75 m above where it is actually placed
findings.failure: shape_fits passes RMat44::sTranslation(at) as the shape's centre-of-mass transform, and at is the body's origin. Jolt places every shape around its centre of mass. The lying RotatedTranslatedShape's centre of mass is (0,-0.75,0), and SetShape keeps the body origin fixed, so the real capsule ends up 0.75 m lower than the one tested (line 2252). The fit test therefore checks a 2.1 m horizontal capsule at her waist height, not at floor level. I instrumented the scratch build and ran matron-heave (the goal's own beat). The test at the origin says it does not fit; the test where the capsule actually goes says it fits. So she is put kneeling where she could lie. In the opposite case (clear at waist height, but a crate, toolbox, kerb or rail foot within 0.6 m of the floor along the fall), the lying capsule is set into that object, and Jolt's depenetration shoves it or her.
findings.fix: Place the tested shape where the body will put it: CollideShape with RMat44::sTranslation(at + RVec3(shape->GetCenterOfMass())), or with the body's rotation-translation applied to the shape's centre-of-mass offset. room_to_stand (centre of mass at the origin) needs no change.

findings.title: The 32-candidate cap is applied in broad-phase order before the distance sort, so a real striker can be dropped
findings.failure: Candidates are capped at 32 while walking found.mHits in broad-phase traversal order (line 2009). Only the survivors are then sorted by distance and cut to kMaxNear. Corpse ragdoll parts are not filtered out: 11 dynamic bodies per corpse, up to kMaxCorpses = 8 kept, in the same moving broad-phase layer, and never colliding with her. Catches and falls leave corpses where she hunts. With 3 corpses within the +/-3 m box there are 33+ candidates, and whichever bodies the quadtree visits first fill the 32 slots. A toolbox or drum that really hits her can be left out of near_, and the blow is missed. Which body is dropped depends on the broad-phase tree layout, not on distance, despite the comment saying the sort handles the broad phase's order.
findings.fix: Filter candidates first: skip object layers that do not collide with hers (kCorpse), sleeping bodies, and bodies not closing on her. Then collect all of them (e.g. a small vector) and partial_sort to kMaxNear, rather than truncating in broad-phase order.

result.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. I read the c780427 versions of the files, not the working tree, which has uncommitted changes. Every step of the claimed path is in the code.

1. The view times the rise from the live stage. `_topple` (matron_view.gd:1147-1150) sets lie_s = DOWN_SECONDS[data.stage] and k = clamp(down_s/0.35) * clamp((lie_s - down_s)/0.35). The `down_s` it gets is down_for_s_, which only counts up (matron.cpp:2394, step_knocked line ~2346). `stage` is view_.stage, exported live each tick (scraperx_simulation.cpp:1596). Nothing in the view holds the stage from the moment of the knockdown.

2. The simulation fixes how long she lies at the blow. take_blow (in post_step) sets down_s_ = down_seconds() at matron.cpp:2191 and then adds rage_ += kKnockdownRage (0.08) at :2204. refresh_view in that same post_step still reports the old stage. On the next tick, Matron::step reaches `case State::Down: step_knocked(...)` and then calls step_rage(dt) unconditionally (matron.cpp:1564-1573). step_rage has no state guard. It moves Pest to Dangerous at rage >= 0.45 and Dangerous to Changed at >= 0.85. Noise she hears while down (heard_level_ gain and spikes, such as the toolbox landing) can also raise the stage.

3. Example: a pest at rage >= 0.37 is felled, so rage reaches >= 0.45 and the stage becomes Dangerous one tick later. From then on the view uses lie_s = 2.5 while down_s_ stays 4.0. Between down_for_s 2.15 and 2.5, k falls to 0. In `_topple`, k = 0 gives _figure.global_basis = Basis(UP, yaw) and the figure stands at the standing position. `_pose` still applies the STATE_DOWN flat pose (pitch 0, arms_splay 1.15, arms out). So from 2.5 s to 4.0 s she is drawn upright with her limbs flung out, while the simulation still has the lying capsule and she cannot catch (caught() rejects State::Down). Dangerous to Changed is the same: 1.2 s in the view against 2.5 s in the simulation.

4. The pinned case (matron.cpp ~2343-2360): when down_s_ <= 0 and room_to_stand(at) fails, she stays in State::Down and crawls. down_for_s_ keeps growing past lie_s, so k = 0 and she is drawn standing for the whole crawl. If none of the 8 directions has room, that lasts indefinitely. This needs no stage change at all.

Smaller side effect: if the stage drops while she is down (for example Changed to Dangerous through decay at rage just above 0.65), lie_s becomes longer than the simulation's time. The figure then snaps upright when stand_up() changes the state, with no rise animation.

I did not run a build. The path is plain deterministic logic, and reading it settles the question.

The suggested fix is sound: export the time she has left (down_s_) and a pinned/crawling flag. In `_topple`, compute the rise from that remaining time instead of DOWN_SECONDS[stage], and keep k = 1 while she is pinned. A minimal alternative is to latch lie_s in the view when the knockdown counter increments, but that still leaves the pinned/crawl case.

findings.title: No way to throw with the BUTTONS touch scheme
findings.failure: Pause menu, TOUCH CONTROLS set to BUTTONS (a player-facing option, settings.touch_scheme = TOUCH_SCHEME_BUTTONS, so _touch.gestures = false). Pick up a toolbox on the 154 m deck. The native snapshot now reads UpMove::Throw (15), but the JUMP button sends &"jump" (touch_controls._verb_for), and _dispatch turns that into _native.request_jump(). Action reads LET GO and calls request_set_down. Nothing in this scheme ever calls request_up, so the climber jumps with the box in their hands. The throw, its arc and the knock-down-by-throw beat cannot be reached, and nothing on screen says THROW.
findings.fix: In the buttons scheme, send the JUMP button's press as &"up" (or call request_up) when get_up_move() == UP_THROW, and relabel the button THROW the way it already reads CLIMB UP or JUMP OFF. Alternatively, give Action a THROW entry while a throwable is held.

findings.title: Looking down, the aim point is nearer than the load, so the throw goes sideways or back into the thrower
findings.failure: flat is taken from the vector between the load's COM (0.6 m ahead, often offset to one side) and the point where the eye ray hits. When you look down, that hit is close: at the camera's lowest pitch (-1.25) the floor is hit about 0.55 m ahead, which is inside the load. Scratch probe on deck 154, facing east, toolbox held, pitch -1.25: the drawn path's first step went -0.049 along the facing and +0.109 across it. The real box left at (0.29,-4.63,-2.80) m/s, ran into the thrower's own legs (player shoved -0.37 m/s) and was heard as a 30 J hit at the hands, which is exactly the hit the throw is meant to keep silent; the Matron hears it. At pitch -1.10 the toolbox and the drum already go about 45 degrees off the view. The recoil uses -facing, not the real throw direction, so in the reversed case it pushes the thrower the same way as the load.
findings.fix: Only take the aim from hits beyond the load: start the aim ray at the hands' distance, or ignore hits whose horizontal distance is no more than the load's. Clamp flat to within about 30 degrees of the facing, falling back to the facing when to_aim·facing is at or below a small minimum. Take the recoil direction from -flat (the real throw's horizontal direction).

findings.title: Holding the thumb to read the throw's arc cancels the throw and turns the swipe into a look
findings.failure: THROW is now an up_on_lift move (main.gd:878). The arc is drawn only while the swipe is pending (main.gd:886), and pending ends LIFT_SECONDS (0.35 s) after touch-down, including the swipe's own travel. A player who flicks up and keeps the thumb down to read the path (the page invites this: 'while the thumb is down the path is drawn') passes 0.35 s. update_context then calls _settle_look(), the arc fades, and the held swipe travel (at least 10 mm) is added to the look, so the view pitches up. Lifting after that sends nothing, and the box stays in the hands. The arc is visible for about 0.2 s at most, and only a quick flick ever throws (touch_matron_heave lifts after 2 frames).
findings.fix: For a THROW pending, do not time out into a look: keep it pending until lift and throw on lift, letting a drag back down cancel it. Or give UP_THROW a much longer lift window than JUMP_OFF/LET_GO and never fold its held travel into the view.

findings.title: Aim ray and drawn path stop at corpses (and sensors) that the thrown piece passes through
findings.failure: Both the aim CastRay (line 536) and the prediction CastRay (line 588) use default broadphase and object-layer filters, so they hit every layer. Loose stock is on object_layers::kMoving, and ShouldCollide(kMoving, kCorpse) is false. After a death to her catch, a corpse lies on the 154 deck. Aiming over it, the eye ray stops on the corpse and the throw is aimed there, and the drawn ring sits on the corpse. The real toolbox flies through it and lands farther on, so the prediction disagrees with the throw. The same happens with sensor bodies, such as the swing's kick bar, which other probes in this file explicitly skip.
findings.fix: Give both casts the moving layer's filters: physics_system_.GetDefaultBroadPhaseLayerFilter(object_layers::kMoving) and GetDefaultLayerFilter(object_layers::kMoving). Also use a body filter that skips IsSensor() bodies, as the other probes do.

findings.title: Heave recoil is cancelled within two ticks by locomotion; the thrower moves about 1 mm
findings.failure: throw_carry sets the player's velocity back by (impulse-150)/85 m/s inside update_carry (physics_world.cpp:561). apply_locomotion then runs in the same tick (physics_world.cpp:619) and brakes horizontal velocity toward the stick's target at full ground traction (22 m/s^2, about 0.24 m/s per tick, now that nothing is carried). Probe: a 55 kg drum thrown standing still at pitch 0 should give 0.37 m/s back. The player read -0.12 m/s after the throw tick and 0 the tick after, a total displacement of about 1 mm. A 60 kg gas bottle behaves the same. The 'pushes the thrower back' heave has no visible effect.
findings.fix: Apply the recoil through a path locomotion does not erase at once. For example, feed it into support_jolt_ or the shove/stumble path as take_shove does, or briefly hold reduced traction (recovery_balance) after a heavy throw, so the push carries over several ticks.

findings.title: The S3 counterweight pig (a route part) is throwable
findings.failure: holding_throwable() accepts every LooseStock entity up to count(). That includes the kMachineWeights pig that lay_machine_weights() puts on deck 8's gangway for S3's brake-trip pan. The new comment on the throw says route parts are set down and never thrown away. Picking up the pig and swiping up (which used to jump) now throws it at about 3.5 m/s, raised, and it can go off the gangway into the shaft. Checkpoints commit on every grounded tick, so the pig's loss is committed straight away, and S3's start loses its weight.
findings.fix: Exclude the machine-weight range: index count() - kMatronThrowables - kMachineWeights up to count() - kMatronThrowables. Better still, mark per kind or piece whether it may be thrown, and leave the pig to be set down only.

result.reasoning:
I could not refute the claim. I read take_blow at c780427 (src/sim/matron.cpp:2049-2190) and sense_near (:1986-2043). A near body counts as a striker if four tests pass: its velocity changed by at least 0.1 m/s in the step (:2075), it was closing on her by at least 0.5 m/s, both on its own and relative to her set velocity (:2085-2086), and after the step its centre is within kRadius + n.radius + 0.25 of her axis (:2093). n.radius is the half-diagonal of its world AABB, which is 0.592 for the drum, so the limit is 1.142 m. Nothing checks for contact. Gravity alone changes the speed by 0.109 m/s per tick, so anything in flight passes the 0.1 test. The horizontal change in the body's velocity is then credited to her as impulse, scaled by m/220 (:2098), and it adds up over every counted tick until 6 quiet ticks pass. sense_near also does not filter by object layer. Corpses (kCorpse) do not collide with her moving layer (physics_world_support.hpp:137-145), but they can still be candidates.

For a pest, a low blow sets reach to 0. She is upright with w = sqrt(9.81/1.05), so takes = fells = 0.2445. A Matron standing guard at the dangerous stage gets the same threshold. All of this matches the claim.

I built c780427's sources in a scratch copy (repo untouched) against the existing libJolt.a. I added a probe that changes no behaviour: it prints each accepted striker and PhysicsSystem::WereBodiesInContact(body_, n.body). The probe uses the commit's own matron-balance setup and the same debug_launch_kit_body call as the commit's "drum rolled at her shins" test, but puts the drum 0.75-0.95 m to her side. result.reasoning:
I could not refute this claim. The Jolt source and a run of the game's own scenario both confirm it.

1) Where the fit test puts the shape. In c780427, matron.cpp:2217 calls `NarrowPhaseQuery::CollideShape(shape, ..., RMat44::sTranslation(at), ...)`. That argument is `inCenterOfMassTransform` (NarrowPhaseQuery.h:53). For a RotatedTranslatedShape, Jolt builds the inner shape's transform from that matrix and the shape's rotation only (`sCollideRotatedTranslatedVsShape`: `transform1 = inCenterOfMassTransform1 * Mat44::sRotation(shape1->mRotation)`). So the tested capsule is centred on `at`, the body origin at standing-centre height, which is feet + 1.05 m.

2) Where the body puts the shape. The lying shape's `mCenterOfMass` is `inPosition + inRotation * inner COM`, which is (0, -0.75, 0) (RotatedTranslatedShape.cpp:53; kStandCentre - kRadius = 1.05 - 0.30). `SetShape` goes through `Body::UpdateCenterOfMassInternal`, which moves mPosition by the change in centre of mass so the body origin stays where it was. The real capsule is therefore centred 0.75 m lower, at feet + 0.30, lying on the floor as the comment above lie_down intends. The test instead sweeps a band from feet + 0.75 to feet + 1.35.

3) Bounded check. I compiled an instrumented scratch copy of matron.cpp and linked it into a scratch test binary; no repo files were changed. The working tree's shape_fits through stand_up is byte-identical to c780427. The run was SCRAPERX_ONLY=matron-balance. In the goal's own beat (matron heave, a toolbox thrown at a pest), lie_down logged `fits_at_origin 0 fits_at_com 1`. The only hits at the origin were the thrown toolbox (body 2425), still touching her chest at y of about 155.1. At the real floor placement nothing blocks, so she kneels where she could lie. The first pest knockdown also showed the reverse case: the floor-level test hit body 1805 (0.05 m deep at y 154.22, about 1 m along the fall), and the waist-height test never sees it. After SetShape the logs showed the body origin at y 155.050 and the centre of mass at 154.450, with world bounds y [154.0, 154.9] for the kneel shape. That confirms the body places the shape around origin plus its centre-of-mass offset, not around the origin.

The striker is usually still in contact at chest height when the knockdown triggers. So the waist-height test will usually fail and send her to kneel, and the lying branch is rarely taken.

The suggested fix is correct: test at `at + RVec3(shape->GetCenterOfMass())` (rotation is identity). room_to_stand uses the plain CapsuleShape, whose centre of mass is at its origin, so it needs no change.

result.reasoning:
I could not refute the claim. With the BUTTONS touch scheme, nothing in the game can produce the up verb or call request_up. The throw this commit adds can only be started that way, so it can't happen in that scheme.

1. BUTTONS is still a setting the player can choose. The pause menu builds it with `_choice_row("TOUCH CONTROLS", &"touch_scheme", ...)` (pause_menu.gd:553), and main.gd:520 sets `_touch.gestures = touch_scheme == TOUCH_SCHEME_GESTURES`, which is false for BUTTONS.
2. With gestures off, `_gestures_live` is false (touch_controls.gd:532). Every look touch then starts as LOOK_DRAG (touch_controls.gd:354). The swipe branch at :393 and the lift branch at :437 are never reached, so `&"up"` is never pushed. None of the buttons sends `&"up"` either: `_verb_for` maps JUMP to `&"jump"`, ACTION to `&"action"`, DROP to `&"drop"`, and so on (touch_controls.gd:258-279). input_router.gd only adds `&"jump"` (lines 172 and 204).
3. Across the presentation code, request_up is only called at main.gd:723 (the `&"up"` case) and main.gd:797 (`_up_buffer`, which is only set from that case).
4. On the native side, `UpMove::Throw` becomes `commands.throw_requested` only inside `resolve_up` (physics_world_movement.cpp:245). That only runs when `commands.up_requested` is set, and only `Simulation::request_up` sets it (simulation.cpp:91). request_jump just sets `jump_requested_` (simulation.cpp:74). `update_carry` throws only on `throw_requested` (physics_world_probes.cpp:446).
5. So in BUTTONS, the JUMP button runs main.gd:713 `_native.request_jump()`. Jumping while carrying is allowed: `jump_started` (physics_world_movement.cpp:978) only checks `grounded_` or coyote time and `!crouched_`, not carrying. The climber jumps with the box still in hand.
6. While carrying, ACTION reads LET GO and calls request_set_down (main_context.gd:344, main.gd:907-908). DROP calls request_set_down too (main.gd:757-758).
7. Nothing on screen says THROW in this scheme. The JUMP label only switches between CLIMB UP, JUMP OFF, JUMP and RAISE (touch_controls.gd:540-544). The up hint is only drawn when gestures are live (touch_controls.gd:720).

Before this commit, every other up move could still be reached in BUTTONS through Jump, Action, Drop or Crouch. Throw is the first move that can only be made by up, so this is a gap this commit introduced, not an existing design choice. I settled this by reading the code and did not run a headless scenario.

Fix: in `_dispatch`, when the verb is `&"jump"` and `int(_native.get_up_move()) == UP_THROW` (or `_ctx` reports a throwable in the hands), call `_native.request_up()` instead of `request_jump()`. Also make touch_controls.update_context label the button THROW in that state, the way it already shows CLIMB UP or JUMP OFF. Another option is a THROW action entry while loose stock is held.

I could not refute the claim. I ran it at c780427 and it reproduces.

At c780427, sense_near (src/sim/matron.cpp:2009) skips only body_, player_ and her own held body. The body the player carries is still a candidate. update_carry (physics_world_probes.cpp:490-496) runs before matron_->pre_step (physics_world.cpp:562 vs 670). It damps the load toward the hands' velocity. So when the player walks at her, the load's velocity at sense time points at her well above kStrikerClosingMps, and it passes both closing checks. take_blow then counts two things once the load qualifies:
- the load's whole velocity change, through the impulse term at :2098, including changes the hand constraint makes
- her whole speed change, at :2137, including what the player's body does to her.

The ContactListener only rejects player-vs-carried contacts, so the load does collide with her.

I tested by exporting c780427 with git archive into the scratchpad and linking against the existing libJolt.a. The repo was not touched. As a baseline, matron-collision passes: closing 15.05 m/s with no knockdown when empty-handed. I then added a scratch test: the heave setup (toolbox taken up, pest hunting within 4 m), then the player steers at her each tick and never throws.
- **Hands free (real play), toolbox carried, walking at her:** the shove lands at tick 1974. At tick 1975 she is Down (state 11), blow 0.3636, knockdowns 1, throws 0. A debug print in take_blow shows the only striker is entity 5323, which is the carried toolbox (BOX entity 5323, 18 kg). Its change was 4.50 m/s, so the impulse term is 4.5*18/220 = 0.364, while her own change was (0,0). The "blow" was the hand constraint yanking the load back after the shove, not anything that hit her. That is above a pest's fell threshold of w(b+r) = 3.057*0.10 = 0.306.
- **Empty-handed, walking or sprinting:** shoved, knockdowns 0.
- **Toolbox held, player standing still while she runs in:** shoved, knockdowns 0. So the player walking with the load is what triggers it.
- **Hands held off (debug hook), toolbox carried:** the striker is again 5323. Her change in one tick is (2.996, -1.485), so the summed change is 3.344, which is the claim's 3.34. The load's own impulse share was only 0.406, so most of the blow is her total change from the step with the player's body against her. That breaks the rule the test asserts ("the player's own body is no blow").
- **Dangerous while hunting (crouched):** the same 0.364 does not stagger her, and fully changed she kills on the catch. So a pest is the stage it breaks.

Net effect: a pest is knocked down for 4 s just by walking at her with a toolbox in hand, with no throw. That bypasses the throw mechanic and contradicts the commit's own rule.

The fix holds up. Skip the body whose user data equals player_holding_ in sense_near, as `held` is skipped. player_holding_ is set right before pre_step (physics_world.cpp:669), and throw_carry releases the carry inside update_carry before that, so a thrown load still counts on the tick it leaves the hands. One correction to the claim: in the hands-free case the shove and the knockdown land on adjacent ticks (1974 and 1975), not the same tick. In the debug hook, the Down state stops caught()/shove on the knock tick.

result.reasoning:
The mechanics in the claim are real, but the outcome is the documented design, not a defect.

What really happens: a pending up-swipe that is still held when 0.35 s have passed since touch-down gets `_settle_look()` (touch_controls.gd:522-524). The held travel goes to the view, the arc fades because `pending_verb()` (touch_controls.gd:454-457) returns &"", and lifting afterwards sends nothing (touch_controls.gd:430). That much is accurate.

Why it is still not a wrong outcome:
1. **It is the existing lift rule, applied on purpose.** The rule is LIFT_SECONDS (touch_controls.gd:67-71): "made only by a flick that lifts within LIFT_SECONDS of touching down. A thumb that goes on dragging is looking." It already covers JUMP_OFF, LAUNCH and LET_GO. The commit added UP_THROW to that list deliberately (main.gd:876-878, comment: "so is a throw").
2. **The commit and the owner's goal describe a brief flash, not hold-to-aim.** The commit says "By touch it is made as the flick lifts." The goal entry says the arc "shows only while the thumb swipes with a load, thin and faint, and is gone on release." The owner asked for "a quick appearing ... non obstructive overlay". The claim's phrase "while the thumb is down the path is drawn" comes from that same sentence about the flick. It does not promise a hold that lasts past the flick window.
3. **Holding could not help aim anyway.** The throw goes "toward what the eyes are on". While the swipe is pending, right-thumb travel is held back in `_look_held` rather than applied (touch_controls.gd:382-384), so the view cannot move. A longer hold could not change where the throw goes. The arc only confirms the throw just before it happens; it is not an aiming mode.
4. **The timing claim is wrong.** The swipe must be recognised within SWIPE_SECONDS = 0.15 s, and the pending window runs to 0.35 s, so the arc shows at full strength for at least ~0.2 s, not "at most" 0.2 s. A quick flick recognised at ~0.03-0.05 s gives ~0.3 s, plus a ~0.14 s fade (FADE_RATE 7).

This is not a regression either: UP_THROW is new in this commit, so no earlier behaviour is lost. Making the throw a hold-and-release move is a design change, not a fix for code that does something other than intended.

result.reasoning:
The defect is real at the bottom of the camera's pitch range. The diagonal "looking down" case in the claim is weaker than stated.

How the code works:
- `throw_velocity` (src/sim/physics_world_probes.cpp:521-543) casts the eye ray from centre+0.75 m. That puts the eye 1.65 m above the soles. The ray ignores the player and the carried body.
- Line 539 takes the horizontal throw direction from the vector between the load's centre of mass and the ray's hit point (`flat`).
- The load hangs under the hands, which are `kCarryHandForward` 0.60 m ahead (handle +0.17 m over the COM, so the COM is about 0.6 m ahead at rest).
- main.gd lets the camera pitch go to -1.25 and sends it unchanged through `set_look_pitch`.
- At pitch p the floor is hit at 1.65/tan|p| m ahead. That is less than 0.6 m for |p| > ~1.222, and 0.548 m at -1.25.
- So `to_aim` points back toward the player. `flat` becomes about -facing.
- Pitch is clamped to -0.9, so the box leaves at about 3.6 m/s back toward the thrower and about 4.6 m/s down. Nothing checks that the aim point is beyond the load or that `flat` is roughly along the facing.
- Recoil (line 553/562) uses `flat` = -facing, not the actual throw direction. In the reversed case it pushes the thrower the same way the load goes.

Checked by running the commit itself: I extracted c780427's src/sim into the scratchpad, built it against the existing libJolt.a, and ran the up_throw setup (deck 154, pick up facing north, turn east) with set_look_pitch.
- Toolbox, load settled straight ahead, pitch -1.25: it flies backward into the player. The hands register a 68 J hit and the player is pushed back.
- Drum, same setup: it also flies backward. The recoil pushes the player the same way as the load.
- Pitch -1.20: both throw forward normally.
- Load still offset to one side after the turn, pitch -1.25: the toolbox goes about 70 degrees off the facing, across the thrower's front, and brushes him. This matches the claim's (0.29,-4.63,-2.80).

Weaker parts of the claim:
- At -1.10 the box is about 46 degrees off the facing, but it lands exactly on the looked-at floor point, (0.86,0.02) relative to the player against an aim of (0.84,0). That matches the stated design ("toward what the eyes are on, from the load in the hands"), so it is not itself a defect.
- The "heard" point is minor. The landing (about 350 J) is heard anyway, and the extra hit at the hands only adds to it.

The backward throw at the camera's own lower limit, with the box hitting the thrower and recoil in the wrong direction, does happen. The suggested fix applies: ignore hits whose horizontal distance is no more than the load's (or start the ray beyond the hands), fall back to the facing when `to_aim`·facing is at or below a small minimum, and take the recoil from -flat.
